html:
The teachings and way of life of the followers of Pythagoras, which began at Croton in southern Italy in the late 6th century BCE.

Pythagoreans held that number is the key to the world. They found that musical harmonies follow simple ratios: the octave is 2 to 1, the fifth 3 to 2. They also believed the soul is immortal and reborn in other bodies, so they followed rules on diet and purity and kept their teachings secret. Later sources split them into those who kept the rules and those who studied mathematics.

After the community at Croton was attacked, the members scattered across Greek Italy. Later Pythagoreans included Philolaus, who said the Earth moves around a central fire, and Archytas of Tarentum, a friend of Plato. Legend says a member who revealed that some lengths cannot be written as ratios of whole numbers was drowned.

Plato took much from them, and through the Academy and later Neopythagoreans their ideas on number, harmony and the soul ran through ancient and medieval thought.
sum: The teachings and way of life of the followers of Pythagoras, which began at Croton in southern Italy in the late 6th century BCE.
